    Citations within a fixed window after publication

    Source: R/citation-window.R
    sm_citation_window.Rd

    Counts each work's citations in its publication year and the window years after it, from the yearly citation counts of the corpus (citations_by_year, written by the OpenAlex readers and sm_enrich_openalex_impact()), and says whether the counts cover the whole window. Fixed windows compare old and recent works fairly, which cited_by_count (all citations up to now) does not.

    Usage

    sm_citation_window(corpus, window = 3L, call = rlang::caller_env())

    Arguments

    corpus

    An sm_corpus.

    window

    Number of years after the publication year, a whole number of 0 or more (default 3). The window runs from the publication year through the publication year plus window, so it spans window + 1 calendar years: window = 3 counts the citations of a work from 2020 in 2020 to 2023.

    call

    Caller environment for error reporting.

    Value

    A tibble with one row per work, in the order of corpus$works: work_id (character), year (integer, the publication year), window (integer), citations (integer) and complete (logical). A corpus without works gives a 0-row tibble with these columns.

    Details

    OpenAlex gives the citations of the ten most recent years only (its counts_by_year: the year of the counts and the nine before it), and leaves out the years without citations. A year missing from citations_by_year therefore counts 0 for a work that has yearly counts. The date of the counts is works$citations_as_of (the day OpenAlex last updated the record, or of the fetch); its year is still running, so it counts as partial. A corpus restored with sm_corpus_from_tables() may hold this date as a day count (days since 1970-01-01, as SQLite keeps dates) or as ISO 8601 text; both are read as the date they stand for.

    A window is complete when the work has a publication year and yearly counts with a known date, its first year (the publication year) is no earlier than nine years before the year of the counts, and its last year is before the year of the counts. Otherwise complete is FALSE and citations is a lower bound: the citations the counts hold for the window years. A work without a publication year, or without yearly counts (no rows in citations_by_year and no citations_as_of), gets citations = NA.

    The result depends only on the corpus, never on today's date, so it is the same in every session. A corpus without citations_by_year gives NA for every work, with one message (class scimapR_no_citations_by_year) that points to sm_enrich_openalex_impact().

    See also

    sm_citation_maturity(), sm_enrich_openalex_impact()

    Other counting: sm_citation_maturity(), sm_count(), sm_metric_summary()

    Examples

    works <- data.frame(
  work_id = c("W1", "W2", "W3"),
  title = c("Early work", "Recent work", "Unknown counts"),
  year = c(2018L, 2024L, 2019L),
  citations_as_of = as.Date(c("2026-10-17", "2026-10-17", NA))
)
yearly <- data.frame(
  work_id = c("W1", "W1", "W1", "W2"),
  year = c(2018L, 2019L, 2021L, 2025L),
  cited_by_count = c(2L, 5L, 4L, 3L)
)
corpus <- sm_corpus_from_tables(
  list(works = works, citations_by_year = yearly)
)
#> ℹ works: filled missing column doi, abstract, type, source_id, cited_by_count,
#>   oa_status, language, pmid, arxiv_id, openalex_id, is_retracted,
#>   retraction_date, and last_refreshed with typed `NA`.
sm_citation_window(corpus, window = 3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   work_id  year window citations complete
#>   <chr>   <int>  <int>     <int> <lgl>   
#> 1 W1       2018      3        11 TRUE    
#> 2 W2       2024      3         3 FALSE   
#> 3 W3       2019      3        NA FALSE
